articles.title: ‘For the first time I have my own chair’: Gaza siblings find new freedom
articles.summary: In Gaza, 10-year-old Anas is one of three siblings born without legs and with only two fingers on each of their hands. They struggle to move around and perform daily activities like eating and writing independently.
articles.content:
With funding from the UN’s aid coordination office (OCHA), and despite the ongoing violence across the Gaza Strip, the international non-governmental organisation EducAid helped the three siblings get customised devices to help them meet their daily needs.

Anas: ‘I’m very happy’

Before receiving support, Anas relied heavily on crawling using his hands, and his mother often had to carry him.

Writing and eating were also particularly challenging due to poor balance and limited hand grip.

EducAid upgraded his wheelchair, adding a detachable wheelchair table and an adaptive waterproof protector shield for his lower body.

© EducAid

He also received a customised pen grip and an adjustable slant table which enabled him to study more easily, along with hand-walking aids which allow him to move around more independently.

“I am very happy and I love you so much,” he told the support team.

His mother was also very grateful for these upgrades.

“Today, these assistive tools have helped him become more independent, especially with writing and eating,” she said.

Sujood: ‘I feel that someone cares about me’

Sujood, Anas’ older sister, is a 17-year-old girl with similar disabilities. She was also born without legs and with only two fingers on each hand, which greatly inhibited her mobility and independence.

To address these issues, EducAid provided a comprehensive set of solutions, including a size-40 wheelchair, fitted with a detachable dining table, and an adjustable slant table for daily use.

“For the first time I have my own chair. I slept in it so that none of my siblings would take it from me,” Sujood said. “I feel that someone cares about me.”

© EducAid

In addition, as with her brother Anas, she received an adaptive lower body waterproof protector shield and hand support walking aid to help her move around and protect her hands when she does so.

Before these devices, writing was exhausting and required her to lie down. With the new chair and table, she can write comfortably.

“This chair will help me achieve my dreams and study the field I love – which is media. Now I can move outside the tent without messing up my clothes,” she said.

Mohammad: ‘My clothes no longer get dirty’

15-year-old Mohammad was also born without legs and with only two fingers on each hand.

EducAid studied his needs both in school and home environments and designed and produced a range of customised devices in their workshops and laboratories to address the particular challenges he faces.

One of the final products was a specially adapted wheelchair with a skateboard, which Mohammad loves for his mobility.

“The hand grips protect Mohammad’s hands from wounds, slipping, and the hardship of crawling,” said his mother. “The table is very helpful, and he was very happy using the small skateboard chair. The commode chair made a huge difference.”

© EducAid

Like his sister Sujood, he enjoys his greater freedom of movement.

“I am very happy with the table – my clothes no longer get dirty,” he said.

“The children are distinguished in learning, they are eager to study, and they truly deserve a chance,” said their teacher, who noted that the children had “started writing more effectively”.

You can help children like Anas, Sujood and Mohammad enjoy their childhood and achieve their full potential by contributing here.

articles.personality_title: Customized wheelchairs bring new independence to Gaza siblings
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – In Gaza, three siblings born without legs and with only two fingers on each hand faced daily challenges moving, eating, and writing. Their disabilities made simple tasks very hard, and ongoing conflict made life even tougher.

**What happened** – With funding from the United Nations’ aid office (OCHA), the group EducAid created special wheelchairs and tools just for the siblings. These included wheelchairs with tables, waterproof shields, hand grips, and walking aids to help them move and study more easily.

**Impact** – The devices gave the children new freedom. Ten-year-old Anas no longer needs to crawl or be carried by his mother. His sister Sujood now has her own chair and can write comfortably for the first time. Their brother Mohammad uses a wheelchair with a skateboard to move around without dirtying his clothes. Their teacher noticed they are learning better and more eagerly.

**What's next step** – EducAid and partners hope to continue providing such customized support to other children with disabilities in Gaza. This helps them gain independence and improve their education despite difficult conditions.

articles.personality_title_fr: Des fauteuils roulants adaptés offrent plus d’indépendance à des frères et sœurs à Gaza
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – À Gaza, trois frères et sœurs nés sans jambes et avec seulement deux doigts à chaque main avaient du mal à se déplacer, manger et écrire. Leurs handicaps rendaient les tâches simples très difficiles, et le conflit rendait la vie encore plus dure.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Avec le financement du bureau de coordination des secours de l’ONU (OCHA), l’organisation EducAid a fabriqué des fauteuils roulants et outils spéciaux adaptés aux besoins des enfants. Ils ont reçu des fauteuils avec tables, protections imperméables, poignées pour les mains et aides à la marche pour mieux bouger et étudier.

**Impact** – Ces équipements ont donné aux enfants plus de liberté. Anas, 10 ans, ne rampe plus et n’a plus besoin que sa mère le porte. Sa sœur Sujood a enfin son propre fauteuil et peut écrire plus facilement. Leur frère Mohammad utilise un fauteuil avec un petit skateboard pour se déplacer sans salir ses vêtements. Leur enseignant a remarqué qu’ils apprennent mieux et avec plus d’enthousiasme.

**Prochaine étape** – EducAid et ses partenaires souhaitent continuer à offrir ce type d’aide sur mesure à d’autres enfants handicapés à Gaza pour qu’ils gagnent en autonomie et progressent dans leurs études malgré les difficultés.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Des fauteuils roulants et outils adaptés ont aidé trois frères et sœurs à Gaza à devenir plus indépendants et à mieux apprendre malgré leur handicap et leur environnement difficile.
articles.personality_title_es: Sillas de ruedas personalizadas brindan nueva independencia a hermanos en Gaza
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – En Gaza, tres hermanos nacieron sin piernas y con solo dos dedos en cada mano, lo que dificultaba moverse, comer y escribir. Sus discapacidades hacían que tareas simples fueran muy difíciles, y el conflicto hacía la vida aún más dura.

**Qué pasó** – Con fondos de la oficina de coordinación de ayuda de la ONU (OCHA), la organización EducAid creó sillas de ruedas y herramientas especiales adaptadas para ellos. Recibieron sillas con mesas, protectores impermeables, agarraderas para las manos y ayudas para caminar, que les permiten moverse y estudiar con más facilidad.

**Impacto** – Los dispositivos les dieron nueva libertad. Anas, de 10 años, ya no necesita arrastrarse ni que su madre lo cargue. Su hermana Sujood tiene su propia silla y puede escribir cómodamente. Su hermano Mohammad usa una silla con un pequeño monopatín para moverse sin ensuciar su ropa. Su maestro notó que aprenden mejor y con más ganas.

**Próximo paso** – EducAid y sus socios esperan seguir apoyando a otros niños con discapacidades en Gaza con ayudas personalizadas para que ganen independencia y mejoren su educación pese a las dificultades.

**Resumen en una frase** – Sillas de ruedas y herramientas personalizadas han ayudado a tres hermanos en Gaza a vivir con más independencia y aprender mejor a pesar de sus discapacidades y el entorno difícil.

articles.title: Veterans shouldn't sleep rough this Christmas, Burnham says
articles.summary: Downing Street says the prime minister will personally write to councils on Armistice Day to urge them to draw up plans.
articles.content:
Burnham will ask local authorities to use part of the additional £874m already announced to tackle homelessness specifically for housing veterans.

"People who stepped forward prepared to put their lives on the line for the rest of us should never lack a roof over their head," Burnham said in a statement issued on Saturday.

"When they need help, the country owes them more than warm words. It owes them a bed every night, a proper plan and someone in their corner from day one."

The PM will ask councils to work with local organisations and charities to tackle homelessness amongst veterans.

Downing Street said an additional £8.7m in funding would be allocated to eight organisations across the UK to help housing providers offer assistance to veterans with complex needs, including those with health or addiction problems.

Among them are Veteran Housing Scotland, Launchpad and SSAFA, the Armed Forces Charity.

The pledge, announced ahead of Remembrance Sunday, is part of Burnham's wider plan to offer everyone currently sleeping rough a bed this winter.

The most recent official figures estimated that there were 4,793 people sleeping rough, external on a single night in autumn 2025 in England - a record high. The number of people recorded as sleeping rough has been on the rise since 2021.

The government has committed £4.4bn in total to end rough sleeping.

Burnham previously faced criticism from the Conservatives for failing to end rough sleeping while he was the mayor of Greater Manchester.

He argued that Manchester's scheme attracted rough sleepers from the surrounding regions, adding that "it's only if everywhere does it at the same level that you can actually end rough sleeping".

Liberal Democrats defence spokesman James MacCleary MP said the funding was an "important first step" but that "a one-off cash injection won't fix a crisis years in the making".

He urged Burnham to guarantee long-term funding for councils to tackle homelessness "for good" and to put in place measures to prevent veterans "falling through the cracks in the first place".

The prime minister is urging any veterans who are sleeping rough, or those supporting them, to call a UK-wide helpline on 0800 9520774 to be connected directly to housing and other specialist support.

Separately on Sunday, the culture secretary set out the UK's renewed participation in the EU's Erasmus programme of educational and cultural exchanges for young people after six years.

The UK will rejoin the programme in January, enabling students and other young people to study, train or get work experience in the EU.

In the announcement, Nandy added: "As we remember the immense courage of those who served our country, we honour them by building the best opportunities for the next generation through closeness and collaboration with our allies."

Conservative Party chairman Kevin Hollinrake responded by saying veterans had not fought for a "student exchange scheme".

He argued that it was "tone deaf and frankly shameful" to announce this on Remembrance Sunday.

"It is not a day for a Labour minister to try to make an EU membership pitch," the Tory chairman added.
articles.reasoning: The article reports a significant government commitment to tackle veteran homelessness by urging local councils to allocate specific funding and resources, including an additional £8.7m to organizations supporting veterans with complex needs. This initiative addresses a serious social issue with broad public impact and includes concrete plans and funding, demonstrating a meaningful positive change for a vulnerable population.
articles.personality_title: UK government pledges new funding to end veteran homelessness this winter
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Many veterans in the UK face homelessness, sleeping rough on the streets. The number of people sleeping rough has been rising, reaching a record high in recent years. The government has committed billions to end rough sleeping but veterans remain a vulnerable group.

**What happened** – Prime Minister Burnham announced plans for local councils to use part of an extra £874 million funding to specifically help homeless veterans. He also said £8.7 million will be given to charities supporting veterans with complex problems like health and addiction. This announcement came just before Remembrance Sunday, a day to honor those who served in the armed forces.

**Impact** – This is the first time the government has set aside special funds to focus on veterans' homelessness. It means veterans can get more tailored help, including a safe place to stay and support from local organizations. The promise to provide a bed every night for veterans shows a serious effort to improve their lives.

**What's next step** – Councils will work with charities and local groups to create plans and use the funding to help veterans. Veterans or people helping them can call a special helpline to get support. The government hopes this will be the start of ending homelessness among veterans for good.

**One-sentence takeaway** – The UK government is dedicating new money and support to ensure homeless veterans have a safe place to sleep this winter and receive the help they need.
articles.personality_title_fr: Le gouvernement britannique promet un nouveau financement pour mettre fin à l'itinérance des anciens combattants cet hiver
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – De nombreux anciens combattants au Royaume-Uni sont sans abri, dormant dans la rue. Le nombre de personnes sans domicile a augmenté, atteignant un niveau record ces dernières années. Le gouvernement a engagé des milliards pour mettre fin à l'itinérance, mais les anciens combattants restent un groupe vulnérable.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Le Premier ministre Burnham a annoncé que les conseils locaux utiliseront une partie d'un financement supplémentaire de 874 millions de livres pour aider spécifiquement les anciens combattants sans abri. Il a également déclaré que 8,7 millions de livres seront versés à des associations soutenant les anciens combattants ayant des problèmes complexes comme la santé et la dépendance. Cette annonce a été faite juste avant le dimanche du Souvenir, jour pour honorer ceux qui ont servi dans les forces armées.

**Impact** – C'est la première fois que le gouvernement réserve des fonds spéciaux pour se concentrer sur l'itinérance des anciens combattants. Cela signifie que les anciens combattants peuvent recevoir une aide plus adaptée, y compris un endroit sûr pour dormir et un soutien des organisations locales. La promesse d'offrir un lit chaque nuit aux anciens combattants montre un effort sérieux pour améliorer leur vie.

**Prochaine étape** – Les conseils travailleront avec des associations et des groupes locaux pour créer des plans et utiliser le financement pour aider les anciens combattants. Les anciens combattants ou leurs aidants peuvent appeler une ligne d'assistance spéciale pour obtenir du soutien. Le gouvernement espère que ce sera le début de la fin de l'itinérance chez les anciens combattants.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Le gouvernement britannique consacre de nouveaux fonds et un soutien pour garantir que les anciens combattants sans abri aient un endroit sûr où dormir cet hiver et reçoivent l'aide dont ils ont besoin.
articles.personality_title_es: El gobierno del Reino Unido promete nuevos fondos para acabar con la falta de hogar de veteranos este invierno
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Muchos veteranos en el Reino Unido enfrentan la falta de hogar, durmiendo en las calles. El número de personas sin hogar ha aumentado, alcanzando un récord en los últimos años. El gobierno ha comprometido miles de millones para acabar con la falta de hogar, pero los veteranos siguen siendo un grupo vulnerable.

**Qué pasó** – El primer ministro Burnham anunció que los ayuntamientos usarán parte de un fondo extra de 874 millones de libras para ayudar específicamente a los veteranos sin hogar. También dijo que se destinarán 8,7 millones de libras a organizaciones que apoyan a veteranos con problemas complejos como salud y adicciones. Este anuncio se hizo justo antes del Domingo del Recuerdo, día para honrar a quienes sirvieron en las fuerzas armadas.

**Impacto** – Es la primera vez que el gobierno asigna fondos especiales para enfocarse en la falta de hogar de veteranos. Esto significa que los veteranos pueden recibir ayuda más personalizada, incluyendo un lugar seguro para dormir y apoyo de organizaciones locales. La promesa de ofrecer una cama cada noche a los veteranos muestra un esfuerzo serio para mejorar sus vidas.

**Próximo paso** – Los ayuntamientos trabajarán con organizaciones y grupos locales para crear planes y usar los fondos para ayudar a los veteranos. Los veteranos o quienes los apoyan pueden llamar a una línea directa especial para recibir ayuda. El gobierno espera que esto sea el comienzo para acabar con la falta de hogar entre los veteranos.

**Frase resumen** – El gobierno del Reino Unido dedica nuevos fondos y apoyo para asegurar que los veteranos sin hogar tengan un lugar seguro donde dormir este invierno y reciban la ayuda que necesitan.
